# 7 Days to Die Dedicated Server Setup Details

## SteamCMD App ID & Commands
The dedicated server uses **Steam app 294420** (separate from the game client at app 251570). Install with:
```
app_update 294420 validate
```

For experimental branches, append the beta flag:
```
app_update 294420 -beta latest_experimental validate
```

## Installation & Launch Scripts

**Linux:** The guide references `startserver.sh` with a configfile argument:
```
./startserver.sh -configfile=myserver.xml
```

**Windows:** Uses `startdedicated.bat` (pointing to your custom config file).

The document notes to create a copy of `serverconfig.xml` as `myserver.xml` so updates never overwrite your settings.

## Key Configuration Settings

Essential `serverconfig.xml` properties include:
- `ServerName` – displayed in browser
- `ServerMaxPlayerCount` – player slots
- `ServerPort` – default 26900
- `GameWorld` / `WorldGenSeed` – Navezgane or procedural worlds
- `TelnetEnabled` / `TelnetPassword` – remote admin access

## System Requirements

**Minimum:** "4 fast cores" CPU, 6 GB RAM, 15 GB SSD storage
**Comfortable (modded/4+ players):** "6+ high-clock cores," 10–16 GB RAM, 25+ GB SSD

The guide emphasizes: "7 Days to Die is heavily single-thread-bound, so raw clock speed and a few fast cores beat a high core count."

## Network Ports

Port 26900 (TCP + UDP) for the main game connection, plus 26901–26902 (UDP) for Steam networking traffic.

**Note:** The document does not mention EACEnabled settings or specific x86_64 binary names.

I found comprehensive information about these 7 Days to Die serverconfig.xml settings. Here's what each one does:

**ServerMaxPlayerCount**
The maximum number of slots on the server.

**BloodMoonEnemyCount**
This is the number of zombies that can be alive (spawned at the same time) at any time PER PLAYER during a blood moon horde. The default is 8. Higher values increase the challenge but also increase server load significantly.

**LootAbundance**
Specifies the amount of loot you will find in containers. By default, it is 100%, so to double it set it to 200.

**LandClaimSize**
Protection radius from claim block. Example: 41 is default (41x41 area)

**EACEnabled**
Enables or disables EAC. You must turn anti-cheat off for code mods or it will kick everyone.

# 7 Days to Die — Dedicated Server Hosting Research (2026)

## Self-hostable?
Yes. **The Fun Pimps** ship a free, official standalone dedicated server. You do **not** need to own the game (client app `251570`) to run it — the server is a separate free download. 7DTD left Early Access and hit **1.0 in 2024**; by mid-2026 it has moved well past that. Current default (stable) build is **V3.1.0 "Henpocalypse"** (stable since 27 July 2026), preceded by V3.0 "Dead Hot Summer" (June 2026) and V2.6 (April 2026). Console (PS5, Xbox Series X|S) is now at **version parity** with PC, updated same-day with crossplay. Sources: [7d2d.net roadmap](https://7d2d.net/3.0), [wiki.7d2d.net 2026 roadmap](https://wiki.7d2d.net/guides/7-days-to-die-2026-roadmap.html), [xgamingserver roadmap](https://xgamingserver.com/blog/7-days-to-die-roadmap-2026-v3-0-dead-hot-summer-console-parity-whats-next/).

## SteamCMD App ID & install
- **App ID: `294420`** — "7 Days to Die Dedicated Server" (verified via [SteamDB app/294420](https://steamdb.info/app/294420/), [wiki.7d2d.net hosting](https://wiki.7d2d.net/hosting/dedicated-server/), and multiple 2026 setup guides). This is distinct from the game client `251570`.
- **Install/update:** `app_update 294420 validate` inside SteamCMD (anonymous login works — no license needed).
- **Binaries / start scripts:**
  - Linux: `startserver.sh` → launches `7DaysToDieServer.x86_64`
  - Windows: `startdedicated.bat` → `7DaysToDieServer.exe`
  - Config is passed on the command line: `./startserver.sh -configfile=serverconfig.xml` (best practice: copy `serverconfig.xml` to `myserver.xml` and pass `-configfile=myserver.xml` so Steam updates never clobber your settings).
- **Default ports:** `26900` (TCP+UDP game/query) plus `26901–26902` (UDP, Steam networking).

## Editions / versions / branches (SteamCMD betas)
- **`stable`** (default, no beta flag) → currently V3.1.0.
- **`latest_experimental`** → the public test branch: `app_update 294420 -beta latest_experimental validate`.
- **EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat):** on by default. **Must be turned OFF** (`EACEnabled` = false) for any code/DLL overhaul mod — otherwise EAC kicks every client. This is the single biggest gotcha for modded servers. Sources: [wiki.7d2d.net hosting](https://wiki.7d2d.net/hosting/dedicated-server/), [7daystodie.fandom.com serverconfig](https://7daystodie.fandom.com/wiki/Server:_serverconfig.xml).

## Mods / overhauls ecosystem (KEY selling point)
There is **no Steam Workshop** for 7DTD — mods are distributed manually, primarily via **Nexus Mods**, author Discords/forums, and the community **7D2D Mod Launcher** (an interactive picker that installs supported overhauls into separate profiles). Mods install into a top-level **`Mods/`** folder; overhauls that alter code/gameplay must be installed on **both server and every client** in matching versions (there is no client auto-download of code mods). Pure XML/config or server-utility mods can be server-side only.

**Big overhaul modpacks owners will expect** (2026 status per [wiki.7d2d.net mod-status-2026](https://wiki.7d2d.net/mods/mod-status-2026/)):
- **Darkness Falls** — the largest overhaul; V6 Stable on game 1.4, actively maintained (no 2.x/3.x port yet). The flagship "does your host support X?" mod.
- **Ravenhearst** — v10.4.1b1 on game 1.4; complete/playable, active dev wound down in 2025.
- **Undead Legacy** — high production value but lagging (targeting v2.4, TBA); historically slow to port.
- **War of the Walkers** — legacy A21 line, repo idle; older but still requested by name.
- **Age of Oblivion** — last confirmed ~A21.2, newer builds unverified.
- **War3zuk AIO** — the most actively maintained large overhaul on the current (2.6+) line.
- **The Wasteland** (Fallout-themed) and **Izy Gun Pack** — actively tracking current builds.
- **QoL mods:** Server-side ones like **CSMM / ServerTools / Allocs Server Fixes / BeyondStorage / Bigger Backpack / Craft From Containers / Lockable Slots** — smaller and often client-optional.

All code overhauls require **EAC off** (see above). Sources: [wiki.7d2d.net mod-status-2026](https://wiki.7d2d.net/mods/mod-status-2026/), [BisectHosting Darkness Falls install](https://help.bisecthosting.com/hc/en-us/articles/40175787721243-How-to-Install-the-Darkness-Falls-Overhaul-Mod-on-a-7-Days-to-Die-Server).

## Key config file — `serverconfig.xml` (most-tuned settings, with defaults)
| Setting | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ServerName` | "My Game Host" | Name shown in browser |
| `ServerPassword` | (blank) | Join password |
| `ServerMaxPlayerCount` | 8 | Player slots |
| `ServerVisibility` | 2 | 0=not listed, 1=friends, 2=public |
| `GameWorld` | Navezgane | Handcrafted map vs `RWG` (Random World Gen) |
| `WorldGenSeed` | (string) | Seed for RWG maps |
| `WorldGenSize` | 6144 | RWG map size (4096–16384; bigger = far more RAM/CPU) |
| `GameDifficulty` | 2 | 0 (Scavenger) → 5 (Insane) |
| `DayNightLength` | 60 | Real minutes per in-game 24h cycle |
| `DayLightLength` | 18 | In-game daytime hours per cycle |
| `BloodMoonFrequency` | 7 | Days between blood-moon hordes (0=off) |
| `BloodMoonEnemyCount` | 8 | Max concurrent zombies **per player** during horde (biggest server-load lever) |
| `ZombieMove` / `ZombieMoveNight` / `ZombieFeralMove` / `ZombieBMMove` | 0/3/3/3 | Zombie speed by time/state: 0=walk,1=jog,2=run,3=sprint,4=nightmare |
| `ZombieFeralSense` | 0 | Feral sense: 0=off,1=day,2=night,3=all |
| `LootAbundance` | 100 | Loot amount % (200 = double) |
| `LootRespawnDays` | 30 | Days until containers refill |
| `XPMultiplier` | 100 | XP gain % |
| `LandClaimSize` | 41 | Claim protection area (41×41) |
| `LandClaimCount` | 3 | Claims allowed per player |
| `DropOnDeath` | 1 | 0=nothing,1=everything,2=toolbelt,3=backpack,4=delete all |
| `EACEnabled` | true | **Set false for code/overhaul mods** |
| `ServerPort` | 26900 | Game port |

Sources: [7daystodie.fandom.com serverconfig](https://7daystodie.fandom.com/wiki/Server:_serverconfig.xml), [7d2d.net serverconfig guide](https://7d2d.net/understanding-and-configuring-serverconfig-xml-in-7-days-to-die/), [winternode best settings 2026](https://winternode.com/blog/7-days-to-die/best-7-days-to-die-server-settings). (Zombie-speed and a few defaults vary slightly by build/preset; V3.x also added a 150+-option "sandbox customization" layer with split day/night density/respawn.)

## Resource baseline (RAM / CPU)
7DTD is **moderately-to-heavy** and, importantly, **heavily single-thread-bound** — raw clock speed and a few fast cores beat high core counts. RWG map size and zombie AI (esp. blood-moon horde counts) are the dominant load drivers.

| Tier | RAM | CPU | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vanilla minimum | **6 GB** | 4 fast cores | 1–4 players, small/Navezgane map, 15 GB SSD |
| Vanilla comfortable | **8–10 GB** | 6+ high-clock cores | 4–8 players, RWG, 25+ GB SSD |
| **Darkness Falls / Undead Legacy** | **8 GB min, 10–12 GB recommended** | 6+ fast cores | Overhauls roughly double base RAM |
| Large overhaul + full group (8–10p) | **12–16 GB** | 6–8 fast cores | Large RWG + heavy horde counts |

Sources: [wiki.7d2d.net hardware guidance](https://wiki.7d2d.net/hosting/community/hardware-spec-guidance/), [winternode RAM guide](https://winternode.com/blog/7-days-to-die/how-much-ram-7-days-to-die-server), [Pingperfect Darkness Falls](https://pingperfect.com/knowledgebase/671/7-Days-to-Die--Darkness-Falls-Installation-RAM-requirements-and-map-names.html).

## Hosting demand signal
**Strong and steady.** 7DTD is one of the most commonly hosted survival-sandbox games — nearly every major game-host (BisectHosting, GTXGaming, Nitrado, Shockbyte, PingPerfect, Nodecraft, etc.) lists it as a flagship title, and the free official server + free-to-run model means demand is almost entirely for *managed convenience* (one-click overhaul installs, EAC toggling, map/seed management, mod version pinning). The 2024 1.0 launch and 2026 console-parity/crossplay updates have kept the player base and server demand healthy. Overhaul-mod hosting (Darkness Falls especially) is a recurring, high-intent search driver.

## Verdict — recommended default + highest-value wizard options
**Recommended default:** Navezgane or RWG 6144 map, `ServerMaxPlayerCount` 8, `GameDifficulty` 2, `DayNightLength` 60, `BloodMoonFrequency` 7, `BloodMoonEnemyCount` 8, `LootAbundance` 100, EAC **on** for vanilla. Allocate **8 GB RAM baseline** per instance (not 6) to leave horde headroom.

**Top wizard options (highest value first):**
1. **Overhaul modpack selector** — one-click Vanilla / Darkness Falls / War3zuk AIO / Ravenhearst / Undead Legacy, auto-handling version pinning and the `Mods/` folder. This is the #1 differentiator.
2. **EAC toggle** — automatically flip `EACEnabled=false` when any code overhaul is selected (prevent the "everyone gets kicked" support ticket). Pair with a clear "clients must install matching mod" notice.
3. **RAM tier auto-sizing** — bump modded servers to 10–16 GB automatically based on overhaul + player count.
4. **World setup** — Navezgane vs RWG, seed input, and map size (warn that large RWG = more RAM/CPU).
5. **Difficulty / horde presets** — a slider bundling `GameDifficulty`, zombie speed (`ZombieMoveNight`/`ZombieBMMove`), `BloodMoonEnemyCount`, `BloodMoonFrequency`, and loot/XP multipliers into Casual / Standard / Hardcore presets.

—

Note to peer: this is my complete section. Two intended verification fetches (fandom serverconfig direct, loafhosts guide) hit paywall/404, so a handful of defaults (zombie-speed values, `WorldGenSize`) are cross-referenced from secondary 2026 guides and may shift slightly by build/preset — flagged inline. App ID `294420`, current version V3.1.0, and Darkness Falls RAM were each confirmed from 2+ sources.
